title: GitMergeTools
description:
Objective: Provide GitMergeTools under src/git to preview and apply external branches/commits into the current working tree. It must compute a clear plan of what will change, highlight conflicts (including impact on pending local changes), and then perform the merge safely when confirmed.

Scope:
- A new module: src/git/GitMergeTools.ts (and related helpers/types) that can:
  - getMergePlan({ repoPath, sources, baseRef=HEAD, includePatch?, planMode? }): Promise<MergePlan>.
    • sources: one or more external refs (e.g., origin/feature/*) or commit SHAs.
    • planMode: 'worktree' (simulate in a temporary worktree for accuracy) or 'merge-tree' (fast approximation without touching the working tree).
    • Output includes: commits to be merged, per-file change stats, predicted conflicts, and an 'impactOnLocal' section showing which locally modified files would be touched.
  - applyMerge({ repoPath, sources, baseRef=HEAD, strategy?, allowFastForward?, noCommit?, createMergeCommit?, signoff?, autoStash?, confirmWhenDirty?, dryRun? }): Promise<MergeResult>.
    • Executes the merge(s) into the current working tree with safety checks.
    • Supports auto-stash of pending changes and restoration on success/failure.
    • Returns final status: success with new commit/merge state or conflicts with details.
  - getLocalStatus({ repoPath }): Promise<LocalStatus> to summarize index/working tree state (porcelain-style for UI display).
  - buildMergeReport(plan[, metrics? ]): JSON-serializable report suitable for client display with schemaVersion; patches are opt-in.
  - Optional cherry-pick selection helpers: selectCommits/planCherryPick/applyCherryPick for fine-grained control over which commits to apply.

Non-goals:
- No monitoring loop or orchestrator hooks in this story; that may be addressed separately if needed.
- No network services; operations are in-process. Fetch is opt-in when clients need to update remote refs.
- Submodules and binary file patch bodies are out-of-scope (binaries listed without patches; submodules ignored).

Key Requirements:
- Safety first: never destroy uncommitted work by default; destructive operations require confirm flags.
- Dry-run support that does not modify the current working tree when planMode='worktree' (uses a temporary git worktree) or 'merge-tree' approximation.
- Clear conflict and impact reporting, including overlaps with locally modified files.
- Patches are opt-in with size limits (maxPatchedFiles/maxPatchBytes) to keep payloads small.
- Typed, versioned, serializable report shapes (schemaVersion) for remote-friendly usage.

Deliverables:
- src/git/GitMergeTools.ts exporting:
  - getMergePlan, applyMerge, getLocalStatus, buildMergeReport, and optional cherry-pick helpers.
- src/git/types.ts defining: MergePlan, MergeResult, LocalStatus, FileChange, ConflictEntry, ImpactOnLocal, and related enums.
- Tests using temporary repos to validate planning with dirty working trees, conflict detection, auto-stash behavior, and successful apply.
- Documentation with examples: planning, applying with autoStash, and interpreting impact/conflicts.

Success Criteria:
- For given external branches/commits, getMergePlan returns per-file changes and conflicts versus HEAD and highlights local edits that would be affected.
- applyMerge with autoStash handles dirty working trees safely and restores stash on failure; returns a clear result (commit SHA or conflict list).
- Reports are JSON-serializable and keep patches disabled by default; enabling patches respects size limits.

features.title: Merge planning core (getMergePlan)
features.description:
Implement getMergePlan to preview applying one or more external sources (remote refs or commit SHAs) onto a baseRef (default HEAD).
- Options: { repoPath, sources: string[], baseRef=HEAD, includePatch?, planMode? ('merge-tree' | 'worktree') }
- Plan output: commits to be merged, per-file change stats (A/M/D/R), predicted conflicts, and impactOnLocal (overlap with staged/unstaged and untracked clobber risks).
- planMode='merge-tree' for fast approximation; 'worktree' simulates in a temporary git worktree for high-fidelity prediction without touching the current working tree.
- Patches are opt-in and size-limited.
Acceptance criteria:
- Given an external branch that conflicts with HEAD and local edits overlapping the same files, the plan lists predicted conflicts and flags impacted local files.
- 'merge-tree' produces a reasonable prediction; 'worktree' mode matches the actual merge result when performed in a temp worktree.
- Plan is JSON-serializable and includes schemaVersion via the report builder.

features.title: Per-file change stats and optional patches
features.description:
Provide per-file change breakdown for the merge plan.
- For each affected file: path, status (A/M/D/R), insertions, deletions, renameFrom/renameScore when applicable.
- includePatch adds unified diffs for text files only; binary patch bodies are out-of-scope (binaries may be listed without patches).
- Respect limits: maxPatchedFiles and maxPatchBytes; set truncated flags when limits are exceeded.
Acceptance criteria:
- For a merge introducing additions/modifications/deletions/renames, the plan lists accurate statuses and line stats.
- When includePatch=false, no patch bodies are present; when true, text files include unified diffs subject to limits with truncation indicated.
- Submodules are ignored for patch bodies; binaries are never patched.

features.title: Local status and impact analysis (getLocalStatus)
features.description:
Implement getLocalStatus and integrate impact analysis into planning.
- getLocalStatus({ repoPath }) -> porcelain-like summary of staged, unstaged, untracked (optionally ignored) files.
- impactOnLocal in MergePlan: overlaps where the merge will modify files that have local changes; identify untracked files that would be overwritten (clobber risk) and staged changes that may conflict.
Acceptance criteria:
- On a repo with dirty working tree, getLocalStatus reports staged/unstaged/untracked accurately.
- MergePlan.impactOnLocal lists files that will be touched by the merge and flags untracked overwrite risks clearly.
- JSON-serializable, compact enough for UI consumption.

features.title: Apply merge safely (applyMerge) with auto-stash
features.description:
Implement applyMerge to execute the planned merge(s) into the current working tree with safety options.
- Options: { repoPath, sources, baseRef=HEAD, strategy?, allowFastForward?, noCommit?, createMergeCommit?, signoff?, autoStash?, includeUntrackedInStash?, confirmWhenDirty?, dryRun? }.
- Behavior: optionally auto-stash staged/unstaged (and untracked if enabled), perform merge(s), restore stash on success; on failure/conflicts, restore stash if safe and return Conflict details.
- Never destroy uncommitted work by default; require confirmWhenDirty for risky operations when autoStash is disabled.
Acceptance criteria:
- With pending changes, applyMerge(autoStash=true) succeeds for a non-conflicting merge and restores local changes; returns new commit SHA (unless noCommit=true).
- On conflicts, returns a clear MergeResult with per-file conflict entries and next steps; stash is restored if merge is aborted.
- Fast-forward merges are supported when allowFastForward=true; noCommit/createMergeCommit flags behave as expected.

features.title: Merge report builder (buildMergeReport)
features.description:
Produce a JSON-serializable merge report from a MergePlan for client display.
- buildMergeReport(plan, { includePatch?, maxPatchedFiles?, maxPatchBytes? }): returns schemaVersioned report with plan summary, per-file changes, conflicts, and impactOnLocal; optional patches included within limits and marked truncated when needed.
Acceptance criteria:
- Report contains schemaVersion, plan metadata, per-file stats, conflicts, and impact sections.
- JSON.stringify/parse round-trips without loss; default excludes patches unless includePatch=true.
- Size limits are enforced; truncation is indicated via flags.

features.title: Cherry-pick helpers (optional)
features.description:
Provide optional helpers for fine-grained commit application.
- selectCommits: utility to list and filter commits from sources.
- planCherryPick({ repoPath, commits[], baseRef=HEAD, includePatch?, planMode? }) -> MergePlan-like prediction for cherry-picking.
- applyCherryPick({ repoPath, commits[], autoStash?, signoff?, noCommit?, dryRun? }) -> MergeResult with conflict details when applicable.
Acceptance criteria:
- Can select a subset of commits from a source branch and preview/apply them with conflict reporting.
- Auto-stash and dry-run semantics mirror applyMerge behavior.
- JSON-serializable plan/result shapes consistent with merge operations.

features.title: Fetch helpers (opt-in)
features.description:
Introduce a small, opt-in helper to update remote refs before planning/applying.
- fetchRefs({ repoPath, remote='origin', refs?, prune?=true, tags?=false }): performs a safe 'git fetch' without altering the current working tree.
- No implicit network calls anywhere else; callers choose when to fetch.
Acceptance criteria:
- fetchRefs updates refs/remotes/<remote> safely and returns summary info (fetched refs, pruned count).
- No working tree/index changes; respects provided options.
- Errors are surfaced with clear messages/codes.

features.title: Types and serialization (schema v1)
features.description:
Define stable TypeScript types and schema constants for plans, results, and reports.
- src/git/types.ts: MergePlan, MergeResult, LocalStatus, FileChange, ConflictEntry, ImpactOnLocal, PatchHunk, enums, and SCHEMA_VERSION constant.
- Ensure shapes are toJSON-safe, with no cyclic references, and future-proof via schemaVersion.
Acceptance criteria:
- Types compile and are exported for client usage.
- JSON round-trip works for plan/result/report payloads.
- Changes to shapes require bumping SCHEMA_VERSION and documenting migration notes.

features.title: Performance and limits
features.description:
Keep planning/apply operations efficient and bounded.
- Prefer 'merge-tree' planning fast path; auto-fallback to 'worktree' when conflicts/renames or low confidence are detected.
- Enforce limits: maxPatchedFiles, maxPatchBytes; avoid unbounded in-memory state.
- Always clean up temporary worktrees; robust cleanup even on errors.
Acceptance criteria:
- For simple fast-forward or non-conflicting merges, planning completes quickly using 'merge-tree'.
- When limits are exceeded, output is truncated with flags and execution remains stable.
- No orphaned temporary worktrees remain after errors (verified in tests).

features.title: Documentation and examples for GitMergeTools
features.description:
Provide concise documentation and examples for GitMergeTools.
- JSDoc for public APIs and types.
- README snippet with examples: getMergePlan (merge-tree vs worktree), applyMerge with autoStash and includeUntrackedInStash, interpreting impactOnLocal, and enabling patches with limits.
Acceptance criteria:
- Examples run against temporary repos in docs/tests.
- Clear guidance on safety flags (confirmWhenDirty, autoStash) and network isolation (fetchRefs is opt-in).

features.title: Test suite for GitMergeTools
features.description:
Add automated tests using temporary git repositories for GitMergeTools.
- Cover: dirty working trees (staged/unstaged/untracked), untracked clobber detection, auto-stash behavior, fast-forward merges, conflicts with detailed reporting, merge-tree vs worktree parity, patch size limits, and cherry-pick helpers.
- Ensure no network dependency unless fetchRefs is explicitly invoked.
Acceptance criteria:
- Tests pass reliably in CI; no flakiness from timing or network.
- Edge cases like interrupted merges (conflicts) and cleanup of temp worktrees are validated.
- Coverage demonstrates key paths: planning, apply, impact analysis, and reporting.
